To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the effect of habitat fragmentation on riverine fish assemblages was dependent on the interaction of barrier characteristics, migration traits and the antecedence flow conditions that determined the temporal variation in connectivity; (2) habitat loss in conjunction to fragmentation had a negative effect on the fish assemblage; and (3) fish assemblage structure was strongly affected by the presence of barriers that were impassable to migratory species.

the effects of habitat fragmentation on riverine fish are dependent on the migration traits of the fish species, the characteristics of the barrier and the temporal variation in flow conditions that determine connectivity.

the impact of anthropogenic barriers on riverine fish assemblages is mediated by the interaction between migration traits of biota, the temporal variation in hydrological connectivity, and the characteristics of the barriers.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact of anthropogenic barriers on the structure of fish assemblages in a coastal river system.
the effects of fragmentation and habitat loss on the distribution and abundance of fish in the river systems.
how the characteristics of anthropogenic barriers interact with hydrology to determine the effect of fragmentation on riverine fish assemblage structure.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the effects of anthropogenic fragmentation on river fish communities are complex and depend on the interplay of many variables.
habitat fragmentation in rivers can have a significant impact on aquatic biodiversity and that this is most evident for migratory species.

the effects of fragmentation are dependent on a combination of the migration characteristics (and hence the dispersal ability) of biota, the characteristics of the barrier and the temporal variation in hydrological connectivity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
fish assemblages in fragmented streams are determined by a complex interaction of multiple anthropogenic and hydrological variables, with the effect of each variable varying spatially and temporally.

habitat fragmentation and hydrology interact to affect the movement and distribution of freshwater fishes in a coastal river system, but that the effect of these factors on fish assemblage structure is dependent on the life history of species.

the impact of barriers is mediated by the migration traits of biota, and these are dependent on the interaction of barriers with the antecedent hydrological conditions that determine temporal variability in connectivity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the impacts of habitat fragmentation in streams and rivers depend on the interaction of biota migration characteristics, temporal variation in connectivity, and the spatial arrangement of barriers.
the impacts of anthropogenic fragmentation on aquatic biodiversity are complex.
the impact of anthropogenic barriers on riverine fish assemblages is not a simple binary outcome of passability.
